reference.title: Cable Biceps Curl (with arm blaster)
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment, so the data sheet was not read; the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching). The arm blaster is not drawn: no arm-blaster prop exists, so the upper arms are pinned vertical instead.

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you curl the bar up, breathe in as you lower it.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s up, short squeeze, 2-3 s down

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Cable stack load is user-chosen: the arm blaster stops the elbows from swinging, so expect to use less than in a free curl.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then one plate on the stack; slower lowering

cues.text: Strap the arm blaster on so the plate sits across the lower chest with the elbows tucked into it. Face the low pulley, feet hip width, knees soft; hold the bar underhand about shoulder width, bar in front of the thighs.
Breathe out and curl the bar toward the chest; the elbows stay pressed against the blaster.
Squeeze the biceps at the top without letting the elbows lift off the plate.
Breathe in and lower slowly until the bar is back in front of the thighs, keeping the cable taut.
Brief pause, trunk still, then repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning back to swing the bar up
mistakes.fix: Stand tall with the knees soft; the blaster only fixes the elbows, not the trunk. Lighten the stack.

mistakes.mistake: Shrugging the shoulders as the bar rises
mistakes.fix: Keep the shoulders down and the straps loose on the neck.

mistakes.mistake: Dropping the bar on the way down
mistakes.fix: Lower over 2-3 s; the cable keeps pulling at the bottom.
Keep the wrists straight in line with the forearms.

kinematics.norm: Full range: mean elbow range was about 117-123 degrees across barbell, EZ-bar and alternating dumbbell curls (Marcolin 2018)
The arm blaster holds the upper arms vertical against the trunk so the elbows cannot drift forward (clinical opinion)
Underhand (supinated) grip about shoulder width; the supinated grip gave the highest biceps activity in the lifting phase (Coratella 2023)
Low pulley in front of the athlete (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 1 s up and 2-3 s down (clinical opinion); biceps activity was lower while lowering than lifting at the same load (Oliveira 2009)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain in the elbow or shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
The cable load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can curl without leaning back.
Adjust the arm blaster's neck strap so it does not press on the neck.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
The arm blaster is not drawn in this animation (no prop exists); the pinned upper arms show its effect.
modify: Wrist discomfort with the straight bar: use an EZ-bar attachment or a rope.
Elbow pain at the bottom: stop a little short of the lowest position (clinical opinion).
regressions: Cable curl without the blaster, elbows held at the sides.

muscleNotes.biceps_r: Prime mover: bends the elbow against the cable with the palm up. The blaster removes the shoulder swing, so the elbow flexors do the whole lift.
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Prime mover: bends the elbow against the cable with the palm up. The blaster removes the shoulder swing, so the elbow flexors do the whole lift.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Grip the bar and help bend the elbow.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Grip the bar and help bend the elbow.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk upright so the bar is not swung up by leaning back.

guides.label: Elbows fully bent at the top
